messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the RFC, I prototyped a small "gatekeeper" that routes requests to a payload-transform layer when clients opt in via a header. sketch below.

arjun: can you drop the header name? we should avoid reusing X- names unless necessary. also what does opt-in semantics look like? is it per-tenant? per-request?

maya: thinking per-request opt-in first so we can canary. header: `Redwood-Compat: allow-payload-v2`

tj: per-request is good for testing, but we need tenant opt-in too for default behavior. else mobile SDKs will spam support.

sophia: is the transform synchronous? worried about p99 impact.

maya: it's sync but minimal: mainly field renames, enum aliases, and streaming frame compatibility (wrap old frames in new envelope). fallback to legacy serializer if feature-flag enabled.

ryan: we should add a checksum in the header that indicates payload contract version to avoid accidental opt-ins. e.g. `Redwood-Compat: v2;sig=abc123`

arjun: ugh sigs add complexity. how about opaque capability token the gateway issues for canary clients? gateway can validate cheaply.

tj: note — third-party SDKs (node/py/mobile) deserialize at client. If we transform server-side, clients might get unexpected fields. Need a client compatibility doc or SDK patch.

maya: agreed. plan: short rollout with docs + SDK patch. also emit telemetry: `compat.optin`, `compat.transform.applied`, `compat.failure` with tenant id and lightweight fingerprint of transformation.

sophia: how do we handle streaming (server-sent chunks)? example transformation: old runtime sent frames like {type:"delta", text:"..."} and new runtime uses ["frame",{"t":"delta","d":"..."}]. wrapping/unwrapping has to operate per-chunk.

maya: prototype uses a stateful chunk rewriter in the response path. Pseudocode: ```
if request.headers['Redwood-Compat'] includes 'allow-payload-v2':
  for chunk in vstream:
    chunk = transform_chunk(chunk)
    yield chunk
```

ryan: what's the perf hit? can we avoid allocations by streaming transform with a buffer pool?

maya: microbench: extra 0.6ms p50, 12ms p99 on small batch under load (gpux-large). Using preallocated buffers and fast lookup maps brings p99 down to ~5ms. we'll need to test on dedicated infra.

arjun: what about routing safety? If transform code crashes we must fallback to the original handler. Add a circuit breaker that disables transform for that tenant after N errors.

tj: and also a kill switch at the gateway level per region. ops wants that in the runbook.

maya: added: circuit breaker + tenant opt-out + global kill switch + automatic rollback if `compat.failure` spikes > 0.5% for 5m.

sophia: data contract question: if transformation includes renaming fields that affect billing (e.g., `units_estimate` -> `token_estimate`) we risk double-billing or misreporting. ops needs a mapping table and unit tests.

ryan: good catch. propose we keep canonical billing fields untouched and set added aliases only for read-only features. any rename that touches billing must be a hard switch with migration and support triage.

maya: implementation checklist I have so far: 1) header parsing + gateway token validation 2) streaming chunk rewriter with buffer pool 3) transform rules table + unit tests 4) telemetry + alerting 5) tenant circuit breaker + kill-switch 6) SDK patches + migration doc 7) canary workflow in console (button to opt-in tenant)

arjun: add integration test that runs legacy client + new server with opt-in header to validate end-to-end. Also test proxying through dedicated and private deployments.

tj: ops: timeline? how long we keep this opt-in bridge? 3 months? 6? need to propose deprecation window.

maya: propose 3 months canary + 3 months optional opt-in + announce hard deprecation at 6 months. that gives SDK teams time to ship.

sophia: please include a migration checklist for customers: 1) test with opt-in header 2) fix SDKs 3) update infra to stop sending header 4) verify telemetry 5) opt-out window end date.

compat-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for tenant `canary-123` in us-west-2 at 2024-04-03T16:02:00Z :rocket:

ryan: after canary we should run a small A/B comparing latency, error-rate, and token-cost delta. I'll add dashboards.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll open an RFC follow-up doc with the transform rules and implementation PR links and ping SDK folks. landing checklist in PR will include rollback runbook items.

arjun: SGTM. one last ask — let's namespace header to `Redwood-Compat-Optin` to avoid other bridges accidentally opting in.

maya: done — will update gateway and write tests.

tj: cool. tagging @sre for runbook review, @support for customer comms.

maya: end of thread — will circle back when PRs are up.
